Inlet sediment or debris
	Inspect sediment and debris at the inlet and forebay; check bypass.	Inlet level + visual inspection	1.0.0
	
Surface sediment and bare soil
	Inspect surface sediment, erosion, weeds and sparse planting.	Visual only; soil moisture is an indirect proxy	1.0.0
	
Standing water after rain
	Compare elapsed time after rain with the configured inspection period. Inspect trapped sediment and underdrain function.	Ponding depth + observation well + manual elapsed-time record	1.0.0
	
Thinned or displaced mulch
	Inspect mulch coverage and evidence of floating material.	Visual only	1.0.0
	
Outlet and underdrain obstruction
	Inspect blocked outlet, backwater, pipe joints and observation-well level.	Outlet level / flow switch + observation well + visual inspection	1.0.0
	
Cleanout cap and joint check
	Inspect missing caps, silt and leaking pipe joints.	Visual only; observation-well level supports the inspection	1.0.0
	
Fixed-point infiltration re-test
	Use the same marked points, method and repeats. Moisture is not the trial outcome.	Manual infiltration reference; soil sensors are indirect proxies	1.0.0
	
Pile not heating
	Compare pile probe temperature with the configured not-heating prompt; confirm with the reference probe.	Pile temperature probes + air reference	1.0.0
	
Putrid / rotten-egg smell
	Record the human smell and squeeze check; inspect wet material.	Manual smell + squeeze reference	1.0.0
	
Ammonia smell
	Record the human smell check and review the dry-carbon input.	Manual smell reference; no ammonia gas sensor	1.0.0
	
Wet pile or puddles
	Use the squeeze test to confirm relative moisture; inspect puddles.	Capacitive moisture proxy + manual squeeze + visual inspection	1.0.0
	
Pests around the bay
	Record a visual inspection of pests and cover condition.	Visual only	1.0.0

	Check cover, base channel and sump following rain.	Rain gauge + sump level + visual inspection	1.0.0

	Weigh intake and complete the human photo checklist. The photo is not an automated model.	Scale reference + human photo checklist	1.0.0
	
Ambient / no-reheat maturity gate
	Compare curing temperature to measured air temperature; require no reheat and human maturity checks.	Curing temperature + air reference + human checklist	1.0.0

Data and limits
What the pilot can tell us

This pilot compares untreated soil, loosened soil and soil loosened with compost at the same marked spots. Repeat field tests establish the measured differences. A small pilot cannot establish a flood-reduction percentage or prove that compost works in every soil.

Model limits

The shared storm clock runs a reduced-order storage and drainage model. Entered conductivity and test records control infiltration. The recorded compost dose does not change conductivity automatically. The model needs local calibration and is not a forecast or an engineering design.

Inlet, forebay and sock share a modelled path level. Soil shading represents equivalent wet depth from stored moisture. Pipe fill is estimated from local head. Reverse river flow, sediment transport, mulch loss and biological fault causes are not fully solved. The compost model view presents the batch record and its checks.

Field checks matter

Check indirect sensors against a reference measurement. Human squeeze, smell, intake and maturity checks remain necessary. Offline readings stay unavailable. Thresholds and layer dimensions require practitioner confirmation against MSMA and the local authority before field use.

Soil and compost moisture probes measure relative wetness. These readings do not establish nutrient safety, compost maturity, gas concentration or odour. Oxygen and ammonia probes are excluded; human smell checks remain.

Data

This environment uses generated local records, deterministic rainfall and browser-local saved changes.

Map footprints use credited OpenStreetMap geometry. Household assignments, heights and drain locations require a site survey. Record the same marked points, a baseline, the batch and labelled dose, the responsible person and follow-up checks.

Data and limits
What the pilot can tell us

This pilot compares untreated soil, loosened soil and soil loosened with compost at the same marked spots. Repeat field tests establish the measured differences. A small pilot cannot establish a flood-reduction percentage or prove that compost works in every soil.

Model limits

The shared storm clock runs a reduced-order storage and drainage model. Entered conductivity and test records control infiltration. The recorded compost dose does not change conductivity automatically. The model needs local calibration and is not a forecast or an engineering design.

Inlet, forebay and sock share a modelled path level. Soil shading represents equivalent wet depth from stored moisture. Pipe fill is estimated from local head. Reverse river flow, sediment transport, mulch loss and biological fault causes are not fully solved. The compost model view presents the batch record and its checks.

Field checks matter

Check indirect sensors against a reference measurement. Human squeeze, smell, intake and maturity checks remain necessary. Offline readings stay unavailable. Thresholds and layer dimensions require practitioner confirmation against MSMA and the local authority before field use.

Soil and compost moisture probes measure relative wetness. These readings do not establish nutrient safety, compost maturity, gas concentration or odour. Oxygen and ammonia probes are excluded; human smell checks remain.

Data

This environment uses generated local records, deterministic rainfall and browser-local saved changes.

Map footprints use credited OpenStreetMap geometry. Household assignments, heights and drain locations require a site survey. Record the same marked points, a baseline, the batch and labelled dose, the responsible person and follow-up checks.
